fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0001
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: Hi everyone, and then for this I'm the CEO I'm co-founder of Swede. It's a pleasure to be invited to take part in this conversation. I would like to kind of share with you as part of this presentation basically an industry perspective of what we do at Swede and how we're seeing artificial intelligence and machine learning being used to increase the capacities of supervisors and central bankers. In a way to actually have better access to financial data in the industry and overall for the greater good of society because obviously a stable financial system means a stable society as well. And so I'll take you on a bit of this adventure out of like re-imagining your finance by leveraging of where we would like to call agile regulation technology and introduce the concept as far as this conversation.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0002
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: Basically this is an opportunity where we think of what's been happening over the past two years. It is a reality that COVID has been devastating in so many ways, but at the same time it's also demonstrated the capability that we have as a society globally to act and to make things more efficient or to actually make big global decisions. You know, which is basically what has happened with COVID. It's been a very big coordinated effort around the world. So this coordinated effort in many ways is an opportunity to be inspired and to really give us an opportunity building back the world in a better way than where we had before. And obviously our focus as sway has always been around a better world.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0003
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: So we've been focusing on producing reporting and analytics calculations that are usually the things that you send back to the regulator. We've been able to actually work very strongly on data standards where they have really taken the conversation forward. It's come to digital regulatory reporting. In many ways, a lot of our work has been very much driven by the reality that there was a financial crisis. This is a health crisis, but it's a crisis nonetheless. There was a financial crisis in 2008 and we saw there was an opportunity to use that crisis as a way to do something for the better. And so in many ways, the regulation that came since 2008 on the back of that crisis has only tried to help the industry to become safer and more stable.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0004
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: And so regulation in many ways for us as a rectangle basically, you know, breathe regulation, breakfast, lunch and dinner has really been for us a way to open up opportunities and open up the data on the industry. And we almost take advantage of the regulation as a way to free up the data of financial services and we have to leverage other regulation as a way to allow financial services to have better analytics of what they're doing through the realities of what they have to be submitting. And so when you bring this back to the opportunities around COVID, there is a reality that what we have learned now that around this coordinated effort is that firms really are putting digital innovation first.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0005
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: And in financial services, the reality of trying to be more agile respond quickly during the right the COVID situation, the central banks actually asked for a lot more faster responses, stress in scenarios to really understand the situation where they had in their hands, not just the health crisis but also financial crisis. And so all of this has really put digital revolution and digital transformation at the forefront of everyone's boards conversation, not just in finance, of course, but across the different industries, but when it comes to finance in many ways, when we have experienced is that regulation has a lot for innovation, but really now with COVID, it's almost opening the conversation to really make the digital shift.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0006
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: So there you would want to happen in the industry, a lot more accelerated and faster. And so, RackTech in many ways is very much in the spirit of bringing new technology in the financial services. So RackTech is really, you know, enterprise software innovation in many ways. What you find here is that one of the things that we feel very strongly about is that when it comes to RackTech and innovation is that you really need to have accessible data. We have been working as I mentioned before on data standards for most of the work we have been doing in the industry. And data standards is something that we think is essential when it comes to accessibility of data and the financial industry.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0007
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: And the reason for this is because standards actually make software possible. And you know, in the FinTech space, you can examples, plenty of examples that actually demonstrate that by having good access to your data, it's the only way to really understand, you know, patents from your customers, behaviors in society, but also to understand where you are at risk as a financial institution. And so when we think of RackTech, when we speak about RackTech and the RackTech revolution, it's very much about also coming from the right perspective around implementing new technology, new technology very much advocates approaches of open architecture and interoperability and access to data, which is basically what we think is quite important.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0008
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: And access to data really comes from standardization and further approach that really allows for better technology to be built. And you know, if you, for example, combine that, you know, thinking with credit evaluation tools, you could really end up in a position where individuals behavior could even be, you know, analyzed or even maybe influenced in the amounts of spending or saving recommendation that can come from their banks. And this is also why you want this access to data, but you want to also make sure that in some ways, it is regulated quite carefully because you don't want to be in a situation where, you know, people are leveraging of that data to just sell more products rather than actually help customers and help the economy.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0009
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: And so you can see a bit the conversation of access to data and the open data piece being a recurring theme during financial services on the GDPR, for example, in the European Union, you know, processes, for example, that was really they cannot really be entirely automated so you can have this approach of, you know, regulation that comes out, but fundamentally, you know, to get access to data to regulate the data in an efficient way. You really have to understand the detail of what's going on. And so then, you know, you take it as a fact, so this kind of access to data is very much all about automation is very much about the realities of artificial intelligence and how can we leverage of machine learning and OP and to be able to train models, you need that access to data because it's how you actually, you know, get models trained to do what you want.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0010
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: And so that access to data has that importance, not just because it allows you to create good technology, but also because it allows you to really work in the frontiers of what technology has to offer financial services. And so, you know, there are obviously a bit of legislation here and there as the industry adopts more uses of natural language processing of machine learning, you start becoming closer and closer to a world where artificial intelligence use cases become very real. And again, this is where the concept of, you know, agile regulations starts being introduced because as you see very quickly, you know, from REC tech, which is basically our innovation and enterprise software in the financial industry, you end up in a conversation of accessibility to data that then can go and train models for artificial intelligence purposes.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0011
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: So then you start being into a world of artificial intelligence that also really needs to be regulated and observed much more closely. And if you see, for example, GDPR as an example, a regulation that was efficient and coordinated in some ways, but also really missed the mark, I think, in a lot of the realities about implementation that it required for SMEs and for startup, and for scale, and for small tech companies when really the target of GDPR was more for the large tech companies. So this is why to give this access to data to rework efficiency and data standards to really be able to speak about, you know, NLP and artificial intelligence, you really need to introduce this concept of agile regulations.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0012
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: So where regulation doesn't hit, you know, miss the mark, but it actually really hits the mark in terms of balancing out innovation, but also good for society. And so, you know, there is also a reality that this is the concept of agile governance that I was introducing. I was actually presented this as a World Economic Forum in the last, you know, World Economic Forum, there was a person since COVID, and obviously we're hoping that this will happen again very soon. But there is a reality that, you know, our work has been used, right, as an example of positive change, and of leveraging of natural language processing to fundamentally turn regulation into code. And so, this reality here on agile governance, which is actually something that, you know, the World Economic Forum speaks about a lot of, and I'm part of, you know, the council for it, is very much entrenched in some ways for right tech, not just for the financial industry, but it's kind of concept of right tech.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0013

fragments.text: You know, in different sectors as well. And so it is the reality of regulatory technology, also how regulators leverage technology, and not just how the industry leverage technology. And for all of this adoption of technology to be efficient, this agile regulation is very much a reality and a requirement, and I mean that the regulators themselves, or supervisors themselves, who create the regulation need to really understand how to make, you know, the regulation as efficient as possible, being able to do a minimum viral price in the regulation. We, you know, implement them, take feedback from the industry, and very much operate like a style themselves, or that's the concept of agile governance. And so, I kind of wrap up here in terms of, you know, the reality is that we think that in many ways to have this world, you know, not be a notorious artificial intelligence with really a reality, we really need to get to a reality of freedom of information.

fragments.fragment_id: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance_0014
fragments.source_video: 0251_UKF_mivJgvA_(6J) D Paredes - Access to data in finance
fragments.text: So, we're data can actually travel freely, and you know, in a way that is balanced as well with, you know, something that does not jeopardize, you know, the good of the economy, the good of the individuals.
